recipe: Coq au vin with chicken legs
servesNote: 2 portions — Karl 3 : Maria 2, a leg per plate on the mash. ⭐ Maria's next-day lunch is the best of the week: coq au vin is one of the few dishes uncontroversially better on day two.
adaptations: ⚠️ THE TOMATO PASTE SACHET IS NOT IN THE HOUSE — it was recorded OUT on 3 Sep. Use 1 tbsp of the tomato double concentrate from the 200 g tube Tuesday's shop bought. Same thing, and step 8 (cooking it from bright red to brick) matters more than which container it came out of.

⭐ THE WINE IS THE GRAPEVINE MERLOT, and this is not a preference. ATK singles out bold oaked reds as turning tannic and drying over a long reduction — the £3.99 Cabernet on the next shelf is the wrong bottle. Dry cider works if it comes to it, but it must be dry.

⚠️ The shop had closed cup mushrooms, not chestnut. They carry less flavour and more water, so step 6 takes the long end of its range — hold them until they have genuinely stopped squeaking and browned.
⭐ SPLITTING IT OVER TWO DAYS: stop after step 12, refrigerate, lift the set fat off cold, and finish from step 14. Delia's trick, and it halves the hands-on time on the day.

ingredients.item: chicken legs, bone in, skin on (3 large or 4 small)
ingredients.prep: patted bone-dry and salted — see prep 1
⚠️ 60 g, not the whole 200 g pack — heavily cured bacon overpowers the dish
⚠️ from the tube — the sachet is gone
⭐ the correction, right at the end — not optional
1 tsp on the legs up front, ½ tsp at the end

equipment.why: ⭐ everything browns in this one pan — the fond it builds IS the sauce
lifting the lardons out and leaving the fat behind
the legs, the lardons and the mushrooms all rest out of the pan
warming the milk — cold milk seizes mash

prep: ⭐ LEGS OUT OF THE FRIDGE FIRST — pat them bone-dry and salt all over with 1 tsp Maldon. Leave uncovered while you chop; 20 minutes if you can spare it. Wet skin will not brown, it will grey and stick, and everything this dish tastes of starts with that browning.
Oven to 170°C / 150°C fan. Chop while it comes up: onion wedges, carrot chunks, crushed garlic, mushrooms halved or quartered.

steps.text: Lardons into a COLD heavy casserole, no oil, medium heat. Let them come up slowly so the fat renders rather than seizes, until shrunk, golden at the edges and sitting in a shallow slick. Lift out with a slotted spoon; leave the fat behind.

Add the oil to the bacon fat, heat to medium-high. Pat the legs dry one last time, lay them skin side down without crowding — two at a time if that is what fits. Now do not touch them. Leave until the skin is deep golden-brown and the leg releases cleanly when nudged. ⭐ If it sticks it isn't ready; a browned crust lets go by itself. Turn, 2 minutes, out.
Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat — there will be a lot, and left in it makes the sauce greasy. ⭐ Keep every brown speck stuck to the pan; that is the sauce.

Medium-high, mushrooms in one layer with a pinch of salt. Leave until the undersides are browned and they have stopped squeaking against the pan, then stir until they have given up their water, it has boiled away, and they are glossy and browned all over. Out. Browning them separately is the difference between mushrooms and grey mushroom-shaped things.
Medium heat. Onion wedges and carrots with a pinch of salt, stirring and scraping until the onions soften and the fond on the base has loosened into them.

Garlic and tomato concentrate, one minute, until the paste darkens from bright red to brick and smells sweet rather than tinny. Scatter the flour, stir another minute until no dry flour is visible — this cooks out the raw taste that otherwise haunts the sauce.

⭐ Wine a third at a time, stirring and scraping the base smooth after each addition. Bring to a proper bubble and reduce until it has thickened slightly and the smell has changed from sharp alcohol to something rounded and winey. Do not skip this. Unreduced wine is the single most common reason home coq au vin tastes harsh and thin.
Stock, 200 ml water, bay leaves, thyme, pepper.
Return the legs skin side up, arranged so the liquid comes two-thirds up and the skin stays above the surface. Bring to a bare simmer.

⭐ UNCOVERED into the oven until the meat has shrunk back from the drumstick bone and gives no resistance to a knife tip at the thigh joint. Uncovered lets the exposed skin stay dry and the sauce reduce at the same time.

Last 20 minutes: potatoes into cold salted water, boil until a knife slides in with no grip, drain, and leave them in the hot dry pan a minute to steam off — wet potatoes make gluey mash. Mash with the butter and warmed milk, and salt until it tastes like something you would eat on its own.

Out of the oven. Scatter the lardons and mushrooms over and let them sit in the residual heat 5 minutes — adding them now rather than at the start is what keeps the bacon chewy and the mushrooms firm.
⭐ Tilt the pan and spoon off the clear orange fat pooling at the low edge. Thirty seconds, and it is the difference between rich and greasy.

Taste. It should be glossy and coat a spoon — if it is thin, lift the chicken out and boil hard a few minutes. Then the teaspoon of red wine vinegar and the last ½ tsp salt, and taste again. The vinegar is the correction, not a garnish.

⚠️ Bay leaves out. A leg per plate on the mash, everything spooned over. Maria's next-day lunch: store the chicken sitting in its sauce, mash separately; reheat gently covered on low, and stir a teaspoon of water through the mash first.
